title.value: Upscaling and Subgrid Modeling of Flow and Transport in Heterogeneous Reservoirs

name.value: Stanford University, Department of Petroleum Engineering

note.value: Reservoir flows are affected by permeability heterogeneity over a range of length scales. Direct flow simulation using fine scale permeability distributions is often not feasible due to the high resolution required. In this work, we develop and investigate new upscaling techniques for the coarse scale modeling of both flow and transport in heterogeneous reservoirs. For the coarse scale modeling of flow, a new class of procedures, referred to as local-global upscaling, is developed. These methods effectively incorporate large scale flow effects into local upscaling calculations. This is accomplished through the use of global coarse scale solutions for the determination of appropriate boundary conditions for the local upscaling calculations. Global coarse and local fine scale problems are solved iteratively to achieve consistency between the global and local flows. The procedures are applied for the calculation of both coarse scale permeability tensors (k*) and transmissibilities (T*). The T* upscaling (in the context of a two-point flux approximation) is shown to provide better accuracy in most cases. Two variants of the local-global upscaling procedure are developed: coupled local- global upscaling and adaptive local-global upscaling. The coupled local-global approach applies two generic global flows (linearly-independent flows in two coordinate directions). This method can be expected to provide coarse scale properties that are suitable for different flow scenarios in many cases, though it is found that for some scenarios, the dependency on flow conditions must be explicitly taken into account. The adaptive local-global upscaling method applies one specific global flow and efficiently "adapts" coarse scale properties to the given flow problem. Upscaling of near-well effects is included naturally in the method and a thresholding procedure is introduced to provide computational efficiency and avoid the calculation of negative and anomalous transmissibilities (as are often encountered in global upscaling procedures). The adaptive local-global upscaling technique efficiently combines the advantages of existing local and global methods and is shown to provide significantly improved coarse scale flow descriptions, especially for highly heterogeneous models and varying flow conditions. We demonstrate that the reconstruction of fine scale velocity from the coarse flow solution, as required in multiscale modeling procedures, is readily performed in the local-global upscaling framework. The use of this reconstructed velocity for fine scale transport calculations is shown to provide accurate solutions for unit mobility ratio displacements. For the coarse scale modeling of transport, we investigate and apply two related subgrid models: a pseudo relative permeability model and a generalized convection-diffusion (GCD) model. Global two-phase upscaling is used to study the effects of averaging schemes and local boundary conditions on the accuracy of pseudo functions. Modified local boundary conditions, specifically, effective flux boundary conditions (EFBCs), are shown to provide better accuracy than standard boundary specifications. In the GCD model, we apply EFBCs and introduce a flow-based approach to compute the subgrid model for total mobility. We present overall methodologies for two-phase upscaling that entail the use of subgrid transport functions generated from generic local flows in conjunction with adaptive local-global upscaling (which explicitly accounts for the process-dependency in the upscaling of flow). It is shown that this approach provides considerable overall improvement in accuracy over existing two-phase upscaling methods. It is also relatively efficient since the upscaled two-phase parameters, computed from generic local flows, can be applied to other flow scenarios. As a practical application, a flow-based near-well upscaling procedure is developed for perpendicular bisection (PEBI) grids for three-dimensional reservoir models. A simplified coarse scale well model based on a well singularity analysis is also presented. The flow-based near-well upscaling procedure is shown to provide accurate results for the cases considered and the simplified well model also displays reasonable accuracy over an appropriate parameter range.
Chen, Yuguang. (2005). Upscaling and Subgrid Modeling of Flow and Transport in Heterogeneous Reservoirs. Stanford Digital Repository. Available at: http://purl.stanford.edu/zp539qc4745
